events.credibility_reason: Claimed proof of a landmark conjecture with no publication, review or citing work in over six years; later work in the record (Chen et al. 2026, Guo–Tao 2026) treats the conjecture as open; the key Theorem 3.6 proof was replaced after reader questions, and the extension to all primes and the decisive limiting step are only sketched.

The quantifier over primes is not stated in any readable abstract (if only some primes, this would be instances, not a case), and the English and Chinese abstracts disagree on whether A_0 is included; body unread.

events.ai_basis: No human assistance was provided. ... After AxiomProver generated a solution, the human authors wrote this paper (without the use of AI) for human readers.

why: The statement is one universal claim over all primes, equivalent to vanishing of every even eigenspace for every p. Finite verifications (Buhler–Harvey, Hart–Harvey–Ong) are instances; d≠1 and composite-conductor work are variants; conditional results, a talk, and the regular-prime FLT formalization are none. Guo–Tao's A_34 = 0 for every odd prime settles a fixed-index restriction for all primes, a clean case. Qin's A_2..A_32 is answered case on the reading that it holds for all odd primes, marked doubtful because that quantifier is unconfirmed. The close call is Chen et al.: it settles an initial index range only for a density-one, non-explicit set of primes and settles p ∤ h⁺ for no prime, so it does not settle a definite restriction of the question; I scored it bound (a proportion/range moved), not case. Its AI role is generated per the authors' explicit statement that AxiomProver produced the proof with no human assistance; Lean checking alone leaves it unreviewed (acknowledging Ribet et al. for comments is not digestion). Stolin's pre-snapshot full claim is set aside as not credible on several combined F10 signals, not mere lack of review.
doubts: Chen et al. could reasonably be scored case instead of bound (eigenspace-range restriction); either way it is AI-generated and post-snapshot. Qin's scope over primes is unknown; if it covers only some primes it should be instances. The investor tear sheet's Nov–Dec 2025 date for the Axiom result is unsourced and does not change the after-snapshot placement. Stolin not_credible vs doubtful is a judgement call but pre-snapshot and non-resolving either way.
